stem.text: Consider the curve \( y^{2} = x^{2}(12 - x) \). There are exactly two points on this curve at which the tangent line is horizontal. Find the \( y \)-coordinate of the one at which \( \frac{d^2y}{dx^2} < 0 \).

worked_solution.text: Differentiate implicitly: \( 2y\frac{dy}{dx} = - 3 x^{2} + 24 x \), so \( \frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{- 3 x^{2} + 24 x}{2y} \). The numerator is 0 at \( x = 0 \) and at \( x = 8 \). At \( x = 0 \) the curve gives \( y = 0 \), where the denominator is also 0, so there is no horizontal tangent there. At \( x = 8 \), \( y^{2} = 256 \), so \( y = \pm 16 \) and the denominator is not 0.
Differentiate again, keeping \( y \) as a function of \( x \): \( 2\left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right)^{2} + 2y\frac{d^2y}{dx^2} = 24 - 6 x \).
At both points \( \frac{dy}{dx} = 0 \) and \( x = 8 \), so \( \frac{d^2y}{dx^2} = \frac{-24}{2y} \). At \( y = 16 \) this is \( - \frac{3}{4} \), and at \( y = -16 \) it is \( \frac{3}{4} \).
The second derivative is negative at \( (8, 16) \), so the \( y \)-coordinate is \( 16 \).

parameter_draw.task: horizontal tangent point selected by the sign of the second derivative
